answer1_theZoningBlockerIsFALSE.b6sStatedReason: situsCity feeds resolveZoningJurisdiction as the jurisdiction fallback, so changing it moves zoning-jurisdiction assignment for ~78k parcels.
answer1_theZoningBlockerIsFALSE.verdict: FALSE. Zero parcels change zoning jurisdiction. Not few: zero, and for a structural reason.

codeRead: resolveZoningJurisdiction (lib/cad-ingest/src/txgio/zoning-layers.ts:571-575) consults situsCity ONLY when txgio_parcel.zoning_jurisdiction is blank; a stamped-but-unknown key still returns before situs is read.

assembleTier1Payload (artifacts/api-server/src/lib/nodeFacetTier1Assemble.ts:350-384) writes the zoning facet -- the only place jurisdictionKey survives onto a payload -- ONLY when zoning_district is non-blank.

The single writer of either column, flushBatch in lib/cad-ingest/src/txgio/zoning-stamp-db.ts:139-141, sets zoning_district AND zoning_jurisdiction in ONE UPDATE statement. The only other writer, artifacts/api-server/scripts/backfill-bastrop-tier1-zoning-provenance.mjs:131-137, only ever FILLS a missing jurisdiction WHERE a district exists.
Therefore a district without a jurisdiction is unwritable, and where a district exists the situs fallback is unreachable.

answer3_correctionOrRegression_andItIsBO.instrument: MEANING-SHAPED, not internal consistency. Input A: txgio_parcel.zoning_jurisdiction, a point-in-polygon determination against the city's own zoning layer -- derived from GEOMETRY. Input B: the situs city, a transcription on a CAD roll row. One party cannot satisfy both sides. Measured for the claim's city and the roll's city over the SAME stamped parcels; whichever agrees with the geometry more often is the better source.
answer3_correctionOrRegression_andItIsBO.denominator: 533,391 stamped parcels across the six counties

andTheHeadlineHidesTheFinding.48021_48309_48491: identical; no parcel changes in these three
andTheHeadlineHidesTheFinding.why: a net +38,696 across six counties conceals a -12,323 on one. DEV_PROCESS 1.1: the headline had to travel with its per-county split or it would have licensed exactly the wrong change.

theRealFinding_theJoinUnderALLFOURLEAVES.howItSurfaced: the Hays swaps are not a vintage correction. They are a near-symmetric all-pairs permutation: SAN MARCOS->KYLE 2,268 beside KYLE->SAN MARCOS 1,641; BUDA->KYLE 1,914 beside KYLE->BUDA 1,722; every ordered pair of the county's cities present in both directions. A genuine annexation-driven correction is overwhelmingly one-directional. A symmetric scramble is a KEY COLLISION.
theRealFinding_theJoinUnderALLFOURLEAVES.theDiscriminator: the 5-digit situs ZIP, compared between the 2025 and 2026 cad_property rows on the SAME prop_id. Neither vintage formats a ZIP differently, so a ZIP change means a different parcel, not a different transcription. Two independently derived values; one upstream cannot satisfy both sides.

crossVintagePropIdStability.countingRule: cad_property 2025 JOIN cad_property 2026 on (county_fips, prop_id), both rows carrying a non-blank situs_zip; agreement on left(btrim(zip),5).

theRealFinding_theJoinUnderALLFOURLEAVES.threeIndependentFieldsConverge: Hays cross-vintage agreement measured separately on ZIP (53.86%), on situs city (53.2%), and on the normalised street segment (~52%). Three different fields, three separate queries, one number. That convergence is what makes this a finding rather than an artifact of one predicate.

andTheClaimAgreesWithItsOWNVintage100Per.48209: claims whose provenance.parcelVintage is 2025 agree with the 2025 roll's situs_city on 104,937 of 104,937 (100.00%) and with the 2026 roll on 34,966 of 65,714 (53.2%). Claims at 2026 agree with 2026 on 63,806 of 63,806 (100.00%) and with 2025 on 32,466 of 62,867 (51.6%).
andTheClaimAgreesWithItsOWNVintage100Per.read: each claim is a perfect copy of its own vintage. The disagreement is entirely cross-vintage. That is renumbering, and it is what recordRetirement's own basis text already names: split, merged, renumbered or removed.

theRealFinding_theJoinUnderALLFOURLEAVES.aConvenientResultIDidNotTrust: the same test on Travis situs_address returned ZERO exact-string agreement across vintages in BOTH directions, which reads as a catastrophic key failure. It is not. Re-measured on a normalised street key it is 53.9%, and on the ZIP 99.73%. The zero was a FORMATTING difference: the 2025 StratMap drop and the 2026 PACS export write the same address differently. Reporting the exact-string zero would have been a confident wrong claim about merged work. ENFORCEMENT: a convenient result is a reason to distrust the instrument.
theRealFinding_theJoinUnderALLFOURLEAVES.corroborationFromTheCodebaseItself: 48209 and 48491 are the two counties in LANDUSE_JOIN_DISABLED_FIPS_SEED (artifacts/api-server/src/lib/joinNormalize.ts:73-76), gate-blocked because 'a CAD prop_id joined into a divergent TxGIO numbering attaches another parcel's zoning stamp and geometry'. The program already knew Hays prop_ids are unstable ACROSS SOURCES. Nobody applied that to the CAD-to-CAD join ACROSS VINTAGES, which is the same failure with the same key.

theDesignThatFOLLOWS_andWhyItNeedsNoThre.rule: prefer the declared roll only where the row is CORROBORATED as the same parcel; otherwise keep the claim.
theDesignThatFOLLOWS_andWhyItNeedsNoThre.corroborationIsPerParcelAndFree: the claim already carries situsZip and the declared row already carries situs_zip, and both are already loaded. No new query, no county-level threshold, no tuned constant.

fiveStates.no-roll-row: retired (CTX-RETIRE). Keep the claim, ungated. Unchanged.
fiveStates.same-vintage: claim taxYear == declared taxYear, so it is literally the same row. Prefer.
fiveStates.zip-corroborated: both ZIPs present and equal. Prefer.
fiveStates.zip-conflict: both ZIPs present and different. REFUSE the substitution, keep the claim, record it.
fiveStates.uncorroborated: one or both ZIPs absent. Nothing was established either way.

theDesignThatFOLLOWS_andWhyItNeedsNoThre.theAsymmetryThatResolvesTheUncorroborate: a GAIN (the claim carries nothing) converts an absence into data: nothing usable is destroyed and ENFORCEMENT's inverse-A1 rule positively requires it. A SWAP (the claim carries something else) converts data into other data, and on an unverified key that means another parcel's data. The two risks are not symmetric, so the rule is not symmetric: take the roll on a gain unless the ZIP conflicts; take it on a swap only when corroborated.

corroborationSplitMeasured.theShape: 95.6% of all swaps (29,472 of 30,840) sit on a zip-conflict row. The swap population and the key-collision population are very nearly the same set. That is not a rule fitted to a number; it is the number telling you what the population IS.

answer4_acreage_theDispatchsOwnQuestion.question: how many of the 103,913 are currently served as refused versus bare null, per county
answer4_acreage_theDispatchsOwnQuestion.answer: ALL 103,913 ARE REFUSED. ZERO ARE BARE NULL. In every county.
answer4_acreage_theDispatchsOwnQuestion.countingRule: acreage leaf classified on the STORED payload: verdict='refused' vs a bare JSON null vs a resolved object carrying 'value'. Recoverable = the declared-vintage cad_property row carries land_acres > 0.
answer4_acreage_theDispatchsOwnQuestion.theFinding: the program serves a DECLARED REFUSAL -- 'geometry was never looked up for this parcel, unmeasured, not verified absent, and the claim carries no landAcres' -- on 103,913 parcels whose declared-vintage roll holds a usable land_acres, in the same row the payload's dollars already come from. CTX-LEAVES2's basis is literally true about the two sources it names and materially false about the parcel, because a third source was never consulted. A refusal over recoverable data is worse than a bare null: a bare null is visibly unfinished, and a refusal reads as a finding.
answer4_acreage_theDispatchsOwnQuestion.andAcreageIsNOTB6sRULE: acreage has THREE sources and one of them is a MEASUREMENT. The parcel-join ring is a shoelace on this parcel's own geometry; the roll cell and the claim cell are transcriptions. The ring keeps precedence over both. Applying B6's roll-over-claim verbatim would have put a transcribed roll cell above a measured ring, which is a different and worse defect than the one being fixed. The declared roll slots BELOW the ring and ABOVE the claim.
answer4_acreage_theDispatchsOwnQuestion.howMuchOfTheRefusalWouldSurvive: 188,665 of 292,578 refusals stay refused, because their declared roll carries no land_acres either. Those are honest and they keep their state.

answer5_situsZip.question: does anything consume it beyond display
answer5_situsZip.answer: NO. Its only reader outside the bake and the assembler is lib/smartSiteStub.ts:179, which passes it as one of four parts to composeSitusLabel. No routing, no gate, no join key, no jurisdiction, no rail.
answer5_situsZip.method: grep of artifacts/api-server/src for baseFacts.situsZip and situsZip excluding tests, plus a repo-wide grep outside api-server which returned nothing.
answer5_situsZip.consequence: situsZip is the lowest-risk of the three and takes the same corroborated preference. 17,674 recoverable cells.
answer5_situsZip.oneCaveatWorthNaming: situsZip is now ALSO the corroborator for the other three leaves. That is not circular: on corroboration the roll ZIP equals the claim ZIP so the write is a no-op or a +4 refinement, on conflict the claim is kept, and on a gain there is no claim ZIP to contradict.

whereIStopped.implemented: situsCity, situsZip and acreage, each with the corroboration gate, and the same gate retrofitted to situsAddress so CTX-B6's merged rule cannot write 29,539 other-parcel streets on the next re-bake.

STOPPED_AT_THE_BOUNDARY.item: Hays 48209's declared CAD vintage and the 29,404 parcels already serving another parcel's appraisal dollars
STOPPED_AT_THE_BOUNDARY.whyItIsARulingAndNotAJudgement: the fix is not a leaf. It is one of: re-declare 48209's vintage to 2025; re-acquire a 2026 Hays roll together with a prop_id crosswalk; or gate the CAD-to-CAD cross-vintage join the way the CAD-to-TxGIO join is already gated for this exact county. Each has a different cost, a different owner, and a different blast radius across money-facing fields that are live today. Choosing among them is not this card's call.
STOPPED_AT_THE_BOUNDARY.whatIWouldDo: gate it, as the third option, and do it in the same place the existing gate lives so one county has one story. The corroboration gate this card ships is the per-parcel form of exactly that, and it already refuses the unsound substitutions for the four leaves it owns -- but it does NOT touch the dollar fields, which are read straight off the roll row with no corroboration at all. Extending it there is a separate card because it changes what cadRoll reports on 29,404 live rows.
STOPPED_AT_THE_BOUNDARY.leftUnimplemented: yes, deliberately. No dollar-path change is in this PR.
